name: Arc quadrant
why: The concentric quarter-rings from the Universal Tape and Super Visual 700 plates. Anchored to a panel corner and cropped hard by it.
vars: `left` / `bottom` / `width` inline — always negative offsets so two rings leave the frame
Swap the accent ring index by moving `stroke="var(--accent)"` to another path

name: Stripe fan
why: The skewed accelerating stripe block from the Super Fomo and K4 E240 plates. Widths ramp geometrically, the whole field shears.
vars: `--sp` (0→1) is written by the shared scroll script; the fan slides 34px across the scroll
Drop `data-gfx-scroll` for the static version

name: Numeral bleed
why: The cropped 240 / 700. A display numeral run off two edges with one accent knockout cut through it.
vars: Numeral text is live HTML — set anything 2–3 glyphs wide
`.gfx-num-cut` angle and offset via `--cut-deg` / `--cut-y`

name: Halftone drift
why: The dot field from the Item E-180HR plate. Density ramps left-to-right and up; the whole field opens as the panel enters the viewport.
vars: Each dot carries `--i` (its own density weight, baked at author time)
`--sp` scales every dot from 15% to 100% of its weight

name: Plate — split disc
why: The SXG/High plate: two discs overlapping, the intersection knocked out in the ground colour, one slash across.
vars: `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"` — the plate fills any card ratio and crops
Recolour by territory only; no hex in the file

name: Plate — checker ramp
why: The square-built glyph from the grey Super Fomo plate, rebuilt as an honest density ramp: column c keeps every (c+1)th cell.
vars: Cell size 40, gutter 6 — edit both in the viewBox, not in CSS
Reads as texture at card scale, as a rule at hero scale

name: Plate — hatch ramp
why: The K4 E240 plate: 45° rules thickening across the field, stopped dead by one solid accent block.
vars: Stroke widths ramp 1.5 → ~19 at a constant 13 gutter
The solid block is the only thing that is not a line

name: Plate — index numeral
why: A card cover that is nothing but its index. Oversized numeral bleeding left, mono spec column right-aligned against it.
vars: Numeral, three spec rows and the caption are all live text
Numeral bleeds `-0.08em` left — never pad it back inside

name: Loader — arc counter
why: A single accent arc against a hairline ring, with the count set in mono. No spinner, no easing bounce — linear fill only.
vars: `el.style.setProperty("--p", 0…1)` is the whole API
The numeral is `[data-gfx-count]`; write the same value there

name: Loader — stripe shutter
why: The page sweep re-cut as uneven stripes: twelve columns of ink, vermillion and paper wiping top-to-bottom on a stagger. Hard linear wipe, nothing fades.
vars: Add `.is-out` to run it; remove to reset — the demo loops it
Column widths come from `flex-grow`, so it is resolution-free

name: Loader — grid fill
why: A 9 × 5 field filling in reading order — a progress bar that is a grid, not a bar. Doubles as an empty-state placeholder.
vars: Cell delay is `--d`, baked per cell; 0.035s step
For real progress, set `--n` (cells lit) and drop the animation

name: Spec stamp
why: The FIG / REV / SHEET cluster from every plate corner, expanded to two rows with a bar cluster and one accent square.
vars: `.tl` / `.tr` / `.bl` / `.br` pin it to any panel corner
Rows are live text — three max, or it stops being a stamp

name: Crop marks
why: Registration brackets and a target, set inside the panel padding. Print-shop furniture that frames a panel without boxing it.
vars: Inset via `--m` (default 22px)
Drop `.gfx-crop-target` if a single corner set is enough

name: Edge ticker
why: A ruler rail hugging the panel edge: rotated mono label, 25 ticks, and an accent marker that travels with scroll position.
vars: Marker position is `--sp` from the shared scroll script
Rotate the label with `writing-mode` — never with a transform hack

name: Scan bar
why: The indeterminate twin of the arc counter. Nine uneven keylined segments with one accent block sweeping at constant speed — for waits whose length you do not know.
vars: Pure CSS, no script — mount it and it runs
`linear` timing on purpose: a constant sweep is honest, an eased one implies progress it does not have
Segment widths are `flex-grow` values, so it is resolution-free

name: Count-up stat
why: An oversized numeral that counts to its target the first time it enters the viewport, with the accent rule drawing out beneath it. Feeds the existing stat-row pattern instead of replacing it.
vars: Target comes from `data-gfx-count-to`; the initial text is the resting value
Runs once, on first intersection — never re-triggers on scroll back
Reduced motion jumps straight to the target

name: Step sequencer
why: A four-stage spine: completed stages keylined, the live one solid accent, the rest hairline. For a build log or a project-detail process strip — the one place the site needs ordered state.
vars: State is two classes: `.is-done` and `.is-now`. No JS required for the static case
The spine is a single hairline behind the markers, not a border on each
Four stages max — a fifth turns it into a chart
